label: input right after an early "i" (step 1 or 2 of the original phase)
explanation: Fires during the original phase on the token right after an "i", but only when that "i" was at position 0 or 1 (so the active step is t=1 or t=2). The current token does not matter. Activations are strongest at t=1, when the sequence starts with "i" (top examples are about 1.0 of max, in particular "i z"), and weaker at t=2 (about 0.6-0.75 of max). Dev precision is 1.0 and recall 0.95; the few misses are weak activations after an early "j" or "v" and a handful at t=3. It does not fire after an "i" later in the sequence, at the delimiter, or during the copy phase.

issues: No real problems found. On the test split the predicate has precision 1.000 (0 false positives), recall 0.944 and mass recall 0.9997. All 1964 missed steps together hold 0.0% of the activation mass. In the rendered misses they show as 0.00 relative activation (after an early j or v at step 1) or as weak hits at t=3 (0.03-0.06).

The magnitude claim holds. The t==1 split takes 59% of the mass and covers the top quartile 100%. The t==2 split takes 41% of the mass and sits in the lower quartiles, which matches the explanation's 0.6-0.75 of max. Precision is 1.0 at both t=1 and t=2.

The claim that it does not fire after a later 'i' holds. With prev=i and t==3, precision is 0.016 and mass is 0.0003. The dev profile shows 0 activations at the delimiter and 7 negligible copy-phase steps (0.000 mass).

Minor nuance only. The rate for in_tok z/p is higher, but that comes from the near-zero j/v-preceded misses, so it carries no mass. The claim that the current token does not matter holds for the meaningful activations.
